issues.t: Oil pump belt failure and engine damage (recall)
issues.sym: The oil pressure warning light comes on, the engine may knock or stall while driving, and the brakes and steering can suddenly feel very heavy. Many owners report this between about 50,000 and 80,000 miles.
issues.why: The 1.0L engine drives its oil pump with a small rubber belt that runs inside the oil. The belt or its tensioner can wear out and break, which cuts off oil pressure in seconds and can ruin the engine. Ford recalled 2018-2022 EcoSports with this engine to replace the tensioner and belt.
issues.next: If the oil pressure light comes on, pull over and shut the engine off right away; driving even a short distance can destroy it. Check with a Ford dealer using your VIN that the recall work has been done. If the engine already failed, ask the dealer about engine replacement under the recall.

issues.t: Front axle shafts can pull out of the transmission (recall)
issues.sym: A clunk, then the engine revs but the vehicle stops moving or slows down. If it happens while parked without the parking brake set, the vehicle can roll.
issues.why: On some 2021-2022 EcoSports the front half shafts can come loose from the transmission, so engine power no longer reaches the wheels. Ford recalled these vehicles to inspect and replace the shafts as needed.
issues.next: Always set the parking brake when you park. Have a Ford dealer check your VIN for the recall and do the free inspection.

issues.t: Automatic transmission shudder, jerks or harsh shifts
issues.sym: The vehicle shudders or jerks when pulling away, hesitates, slams into gear, or feels like it is slipping. Some owners report fluid leaks or a transmission warning.
issues.why: Owners report wear and faults in the 6-speed automatic, including torque converter problems, often between about 45,000 and 85,000 miles. Ford also issued service notes on torque converter fitting and on transmission-related warning codes for these years.
issues.next: Have the transmission scanned for codes and the fluid level and condition checked. Ask the dealer about any software updates. Catching a slipping transmission early can avoid a full replacement.

issues.t: Coolant loss, white exhaust smoke and rough running (1.0L)
issues.sym: The coolant level keeps dropping with no visible leak, white smoke comes from the exhaust, the engine runs rough or misfires, or it overheats.
issues.why: Ford issued a service note for the 1.0L EcoBoost about engines using coolant, smoking white and running roughly. Owners also report coolant getting into the cylinders and overheating, which can crack the head or damage the engine.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant tank and stop driving if the temperature warning appears. Ask a shop for a cooling system pressure test and a combustion leak test. Do not keep topping off coolant without finding where it goes.

issues.t: Coolant leak from water pump or hoses
issues.sym: A sweet smell, puddles of coolant under the front, a low coolant warning, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: Owners report leaking coolant hoses, water pumps and thermostats on these years. Low coolant can quickly lead to overheating.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold. If it keeps dropping, have the cooling system pressure-tested and fix the leak before it overheats the engine.

issues.t: Turbocharger failure (1.0L)
issues.sym: A grinding or whining noise from the engine, loss of power, the engine going into limp mode, blue or gray smoke, or a turbo-related warning code.
issues.why: Owners report turbochargers on the small 1.0L engine wearing out or seizing. Turbos depend on clean oil at full pressure, so oil pump belt trouble can also damage them.
issues.next: Have the turbo and boost system checked as soon as power drops or you hear grinding. Also make sure the oil pump belt recall has been done, since a failing belt can take out the turbo too.

issues.t: Hard starting after filling the gas tank
issues.sym: The engine cranks a long time or stumbles right after you refuel, and the check engine light may come on with an evaporative system code such as P0496.
issues.why: The evaporative emissions purge valve can stick open, letting fuel vapor flood the engine after a fill-up.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A stuck purge valve is a common cause, and replacing it usually fixes the problem.

issues.t: Dead battery or charging system warning
issues.sym: The vehicle will not start, the battery keeps going flat, or a charging system or battery warning message appears.
issues.why: Owners report weak batteries, alternator failures and charging system faults on these years.
issues.next: Have the battery and alternator tested. If the battery is fine but still goes flat, ask a shop to check for a power drain.

issues.t: Backup camera blank or stays on (recall)
issues.sym: The backup camera screen shows a blank image when you shift into Reverse, or the camera image stays on after you shift out of Reverse.
issues.why: A software error in the camera system can cause it to show nothing or keep showing the camera view. Ford recalled many models, including some 2020-2021 EcoSports, for a software update.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free software update done. Until then, look over your shoulder when backing up.

issues.t: Front seat frame may not be welded properly (recall)
issues.sym: The front seat back may feel loose or move more than it should.
issues.why: Some 2019 EcoSport front seat frames were not welded correctly, so the seat back might not hold the occupant in a crash. Ford recalled these vehicles to replace the front seats.
issues.next: Check your VIN for the recall and have the seats replaced for free.

issues.t: Front airbag may not inflate in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning at all. The problem only shows up in a crash.
issues.why: Some 2020 EcoSport front airbag modules were built without part of the propellant that inflates the bag, so it might not deploy. Ford recalled these vehicles to replace the affected airbag.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and get the airbag replaced free at a Ford dealer as soon as you can.

issues.t: Check engine light from crankcase ventilation codes (1.0L)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes again and again after it is cleared, with codes such as P04DB or P051B. The engine may seem to run normally.
issues.why: Ford issued service bulletins for 1.0L EcoBoost engines setting crankcase ventilation and crankcase pressure sensor codes. A disconnected or faulty ventilation hose, or a faulty pressure sensor, is the usual cause.
issues.next: Have a shop read the codes and check the crankcase ventilation hoses and sensor. Mention the Ford bulletins for the code you have.

issues.t: Check engine light from damaged wiring harness (2.0L)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P06A7, and the engine may run poorly.
issues.why: Ford found that a damaged circuit in an engine wiring harness can set this code on 2.0L EcoSports.
issues.next: Have the code read and the harness inspected for chafed or damaged wires. Repairing the harness is usually the fix.

issues.t: Check engine light in freezing weather, code P0125 (2.0L)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on during cold starts, usually just below freezing, with code P0125.
issues.why: Early 2018 2.0L EcoSports built in late 2017 can set this coolant temperature code in cold weather. Ford released a bulletin with a fix.
issues.next: Have the code read and ask a Ford dealer about the bulletin for this code. It is not urgent if the engine warms up and runs normally.

issues.t: Clicking or ratcheting from the driveshaft when backing up (AWD)
issues.sym: A clicking or ratcheting noise from under the vehicle when reversing, especially up a slope or with a load.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for all-wheel-drive EcoSports built before mid-April 2018 for noise from the rear driveshaft when reversing under load.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm the noise and apply the bulletin repair. It is usually not dangerous, but get it checked so a real driveline fault is not missed.

issues.t: Weak air conditioning
issues.sym: The A/C blows cool rather than cold, cooling comes and goes, or the climate control does not work properly. A code such as P06A0 may be stored.
issues.why: Ford issued several service notes about poor A/C performance on vehicles with this type of variable A/C compressor, including the EcoSport.
issues.next: Have the A/C pressures and codes checked by a shop. Ask about the Ford bulletins before agreeing to a compressor or evaporator replacement.

issues.t: SYNC 3 screen freezes, goes black or will not respond
issues.sym: The touchscreen goes blue or black, stops responding to touch, or phone, navigation or voice features act up.
issues.why: Ford issued multiple service notes for SYNC 3 screens that freeze or go blank, usually fixed by updating the system software.
issues.next: Check for SYNC software updates (over Wi-Fi, USB, or at a dealer). A master reset can help temporarily.

issues.t: Power windows stop working
issues.sym: A power window stops going up or down, sometimes after the switch is pressed several times quickly.
issues.why: Ford issued a service note for 2018-2019 EcoSports whose power windows stop working after rapid repeated switch use.
issues.next: Have a dealer check for the service note fix before replacing a window motor or regulator.

issues.t: Will not start with a Key Not Detected message
issues.sym: With keyless start, the vehicle will not start and the dash says the key is not detected, even with the key inside.
issues.why: Ford issued a service note for keyless-start EcoSports built before late September 2018 that may not recognize the key.
issues.next: Try holding the key fob near the start button or the backup spot shown in the owner manual. Have a dealer apply the fix from the service note.

issues.t: Radio switches from FM to AM by itself
issues.sym: The radio jumps from FM to AM without anyone touching it.
issues.why: Ford issued a service note for 2018 EcoSports built before June 2018 with this radio glitch. It is fixed with a software update.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the software update listed in the service note.

issues.t: Doors do not lock automatically
issues.sym: The doors no longer lock by themselves when you start driving.
issues.why: Ford found that auto-lock may be turned off on EcoSports built before July 2019. The fix is reprogramming the body control module.
issues.next: Check the auto-lock setting first. If it will not stay on, have a dealer reprogram the body control module.

issues.t: Alarm goes off after a loud noise
issues.sym: The factory accessory alarm goes off on its own, often after thunder, a loud truck or another loud sound nearby.
issues.why: Ford issued a service note for 2018-2019 EcoSports with keyed ignition and the accessory alarm that can be set off by loud noises.
issues.next: Have the dealer apply the fix from the service note.

issues.t: Exhaust system rusting early
issues.sym: A louder exhaust, rattles from underneath, or exhaust smell, sometimes at only about 30,000 miles.
issues.why: Owners of 2018 EcoSports report exhaust pipes and parts rusting through early.
issues.next: Have the exhaust inspected for holes and loose parts. Fix leaks near the front quickly, since fumes can get into the cabin.

issues.t: Wrench light from remote start
issues.sym: A wrench warning light and a See Manual message come on, often on vehicles with dealer-installed or app remote start.
issues.why: Ford found that remote start systems on early EcoSports can set code P166A and turn on the wrench light even when nothing is wrong with the engine.
issues.next: Have the code read. If it is P166A, ask the dealer for the remote start bulletin fix.
